etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: Inherited from Middle English precursour, from Middle French precurseur or its etymon Latin praecursor (“forerunner”). By surface analysis, precurse +‎ -or.
senses: That which precurses: a forerunner, predecessor, or indicator of approaching events.

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
senses: (telecommunications, of intersymbol interference) Caused by the following symbol.
